answer: A fresh clone can forge a key in a second, but it cannot forge the one signal that matters: a ledger of quorum-matched grading verdicts, each re-checked against consensus and sealed on-chain. That record accretes like a coral reef — one honest judgment per epoch — and no sibling identity can be handed it. Spin up a thousand fakes and each must grade its own way up from zero, so the Sybil bill rises linearly with the number of identities and is never shared.
